findings.title: Stale distance field is never rebuilt while a same-wave sidestep exists, so carriers sidestep and step back every turn against a wall the field thinks is open
findings.mechanism: Field.addWall (Field.java:39-43) only sets Field.stale when a newly sensed wall lies inside the field. A carrier's field is built from walls it knew at request time, and unknown squares count as open. A newborn requests one on its first wall hit, when it knows almost nothing. Later, its downhill neighbours (wave k-1) turn out to be walls: can(d) fails, so wallDown=true (Nav.java:134-135) and down stays null. But `go = down != null ? down : side` (Nav.java:145) takes any free same-wave square, and the branch returns at line 153. The only carrier rebuild, `if (down == null && wallDown) { Field.request(ft,true) }` at Nav.java:157, therefore never runs while a side square is free. From the side square the same stale field points back at the same wall and picks the original square as its side step. moveTwice (Carrier.java:828-831) makes both moves in one turn (A->B->A), so the carrier ends every turn where it started. Launchers escape this because Launcher.java:392 re-requests the plan every march turn beyond r2 150, but carriers have no periodic request. The c_nav3 design says 'a field is rebuilt only when a downhill square proves to be a wall', and this code path breaks that intent.
findings.evidence: c_gd1 panel (gauntlet/20261020-001652-panel-c_gd1, replays parsed with scratchpad rep.py and stuckscan.py): Forest had stalled carriers in 10 of 10 games. 30 carriers sat on x=5, y=13..21 (the west face of the x=6..7 wall, with the Ad well (9,21) east of it), each still for 100 or more rounds, 9,243 carrier-rounds in total. All were in state G, with about 3,700-4,100 bytecodes per turn (two Nav calls). The longest was 10337 g4 #10780 at (5,21), still 1,110 rounds from r630. fieldsim.py checked 6 of 6 stalls in 10337 g4 (#10780 born r626 stuck r630; #12984 born r126 stuck r130; #10940 born r1248 stuck r1253; #13712 born r1249 stuck r1268; #10936 born r800 stuck r836; #12036 born r1056 stuck r1295). A field toward (9,21) built from the carrier's own vision at birth reproduces exactly 'side, side back to the start tile' on the stall square. The true BFS level is 13-18 steps, while the stale field says 6-12. Ladder: 9913 g1 PairedProgramming #10151 (Mn carrier) was still at (28,0) from r13 to r457 (444 rounds, whole game, lost). Its field from knowledge up to r11 has L(28,1)=8 for a wall it believed open, giving side(27,0), side(28,0) every turn. With knowledge up to r12 it walks out in 3 turns. 9929 g0 Forest #10840 was still 416 rounds at (5,21), with L(5,21)=4 against a true 13.

findings.title: Potions corridor plug: a mana carrier 'near' a well by straight-line distance but walled off loops W -> S -> same well forever in a 1-wide corridor, freezing 15+ units and the HQ
findings.mechanism: gather() treats any d2 <= PACK_R2 (8) as 'at a crowded well'. packApproach (Carrier.java:613-620) walks to packTarget's nearest free collect square by straight-line distance, which can lie across a wall. Nav.moveTo to a target within r2 20 never requests a field (Nav.java:181, FIELD_MIN_D2), so greedy hits the wall and bug-follows. In a 1-wide corridor full of robots, wall-following treats robots as walls (Nav.java:215-217) and only finds the way back. The carrier makes no progress, so line 401 sets W and crowdTurns rises. After WELL_CROWD_PATIENCE (6) it goes S -> switchWell. A mana carrier (ROLES 3, role 2) may switch only to mana wells (Carrier.java:681/691). With none, well=null (line 698), and on the same turn gather re-picks the nearest well, the same one (lines 359-369). That gives a 6-W, 1-S cycle with no end, and the carrier never leaves its corridor tile. Behind it, an Ad carrier aiming at a walled well at r2 10 (bug only, no field) ping-pongs in-turn (33,11)->(32,11)->(33,11). Launchers spawned at the HQ's corridor mouth (HQ.tryBuild ranks spawn tiles by straight-line distance to the enemy HQ) march into the plug and wait. Anchor carriers (E/Y/K, excluded from unjam) end up holding the HQ's only adjacent tiles.

findings.title: unjam() can never fire for an empty carrier that oscillates within one turn: moveTwice spends the movement cooldown that unjam requires
findings.mechanism: stillTurns compares turn-start tiles (Carrier.java:52), so an in-turn A->B->A cycle counts as still. But unjam() returns unless rc.isMovementReady() (line 128). An empty carrier's move cooldown is floor(0.375*0)+5 = 5 (RULES.md weight rule; ready means cd < 10), so the two Nav.moveTo calls in moveTwice (lines 828-831) or packApproach (lines 615-619) leave cd 10 at unjam time. Every oscillation that returns to its start tile within a turn makes unjam unreachable: the stale-field sidestep above and the bug ping-pong in 1-wide corridors. unjam also skips anchor states Y/E/K (line 129), and deliverAnchor/scoutMove use moveTwice.
findings.evidence: 10337 g4 #10780 stood at (5,21) in state G (allowed by unjam) for 1,110 rounds. The snapshots at r700/r1300/r1450 show (4,20), (4,21), (4,22) and (5,20) free, so unjam would have moved it on its 6th still turn had it been movement-ready. Every turn therefore ended with cd >= 10, which means two moves. The same holds for all 30 Forest x=5 stalls in the c_gd1 panel (free west neighbours, state G) and 9913 #10151 (444 rounds). The 2026-10-12 native fixture also recorded cd 0->5->10 and 'the subsequent unjam routine cannot move on that turn'. Anchor carriers stuck without unjam: 9508 #12666 (E=945) and #13594 (E=826) on HQ-adjacent tiles for 1,090 rounds; 10146 #13088 Y=1151.

findings.title: MassiveL gridlock: crowd switches send mana carriers between the two mana wells 39 rows apart through the 2-wide west strip, and opposing streams lock 20+ carriers around well (2,0)
findings.mechanism: switchWell (Carrier.java:672-698) picks the nearest other mana well with no distance limit (line 684 and line 694 only add +400 for another type). On MassiveL the next mana well after (2,0) is (0,39) and vice versa. Crowded carriers from each well cross the map through the 2-wide strip x=0..1 (y=2..12) and the 2-high corridor y=0..1 in opposite directions. Nav has no passing rule. The robots-only branch waits (Nav.java:172-178), the field waits or retreats only into a free square (Nav.java:146/158), and bug treats robots as walls. Inbound carriers queued more than r2 8 from the well stay in state G and never count crowdTurns (line 401; only Mid sites get the beyond-r2-8 queue rule at line 399). Loaded carriers on the collect squares cannot get out, and the queue never breaks up. unjam needs a free neighbour, and the corridor is packed.

findings.title: Island news is published only on 1 turn in 5 at end of turn, so a fresh 'neutral' sighting brought home is lost (root cause of the 10114 incident)
findings.mechanism: MapMem.flushIslands runs only when (round+id)%5==0 (RobotPlayer.java:64). It runs at the END of the turn, gated by the start-of-turn Comms.canWrite (Comms.startTurn, Comms.java:43-45), and put() re-checks the write at the end position (Comms.java:56-58). Only a record at most C.ISLAND_FRESH (8) rounds old may replace a slot that names another owner (MapMem.mayWrite:183-186; slots carry no time). RULES §7 allows writes only within r2 9 of our HQ, r2 20 of our amplifier (we build none) or r2 4 of an island we own. A launcher or carrier passing through an HQ zone is usually inside for 1-4 turns, so the freshness window and the flush cadence often fail to overlap, and news from the enemy half is lost for good. Readers that then act on the stale slot: Launcher.pickObjective (Launcher.java:994-1006; a newborn has no record of its own, so the slot decides), Comms.islandStats (islLocNeutral, which HQ.java:70-71 uses for anchors), Carrier.ownerOf (Carrier.java:833-838) and chooseIsland (an island owned by 2 is skipped).
findings.evidence: Match 10114 game 2 (Cornucopia, ranked; c_gd1 = c_kx0 constants; the island code is unchanged since c_isle1). From the replay, island 2 (51-54,28-30) was held by the enemy r810-909 and neutral r910-2000. A replay-driven simulation of our writes put 'theirs' in its slot at r858 (scout 10721 at (48,20), fresh sighting), and it stayed 'theirs' to r2000. Launcher 13280 sensed island 2 neutral from (50,24) at r932 (its telemetry objective kind changed 1->2 that turn). It started r939 at (46,20), d2 8 to HQ (48,18), holding a neutral record 7 rounds old, but (939+13280)%5=4, so no flush. On its flush turn r940 it ended at (45,21), d2 18, so the write was refused, and the record was then 12 rounds old. No other robot ever carried the news. Results of the stale slot: islLocNeutral was 0, so the HQs built only 'blind' anchors (the wantAnchor bit set about every 150 rounds per HQ), and couriers skipped island 2. From r1525, when the enemy held no island, 240,121 of 342,946 launcher turns (70%) still had objective kind 1 (an enemy island). 111 of the 157 launchers born after r1600 took kind 1 within 12 turns. The game ended tb_islands with 6 islands (7 needed for conquest), 734 launchers built, and 30 anchors built for 7 placed. findings.title: ISLE_STICKY writes a single 15-round-old 'theirs' sighting over a neutral slot after the island has already been lost: phantom enemy island for 1,378 rounds
findings.mechanism: mayWrite's sticky clause (MapMem.java:185; C.ISLE_STICKY=true at C.java:487, ISLE_STICKY_AGE 60) lets flushIslands publish an owner-2 record up to 60 rounds old over a located neutral slot. The record may come from one scan taken the round an enemy anchor was placed. Our nearby army usually destroys such an anchor within a few rounds, and nothing can correct the slot afterwards. A neutral record replaces 'theirs' only if it is at most 8 rounds old and reaches a write zone (RULES §7), which robots in the enemy half almost never do (finding 1). Launchers born later have no record of their own, so they follow the slot (Launcher.java:994-1006, theirsFor 884-885). Comms.islThem counts it, which affects the HQ gate before r800 (HQ.java:68-69).
findings.evidence: Match 10110 game 8 (Maze vs vrangr1, c_adp1 panel; the island code is the same as c_gd1's; 9901 g8 is the same game). From the replay, island 2 (38-40,23) was held by the enemy only r327-337. Carrier 10158 was within vision of it at r327-328 and reached HQ (21,21)'s zone r339-342. On its flush turn r342 the sticky rule wrote 'theirs' (record 15 rounds old) over the neutral slot, 4 rounds after the island had turned neutral (replay-driven simulation, island truth at end of round). Telemetry confirms the slot: of 182 launchers born r344-700, 151 took objective kind 1 on their first turn, at all three HQs (61 of 61 at (3,46), 44 of 50 at (11,2), 46 of 71 at (21,21)). All 19 born r300-343 took kind 2. Over the game, 601 of 781 launchers took kind 1 within 3 rounds of birth, and 397,970 of 521,663 launcher turns (76%) had kind 1 to r1720, although the enemy held no island. Simulation: ISLE_STICKY=false removes the phantom (wrong-'theirs' island-rounds 1,379->0) but costs real knowledge in the conquest loss 10340 g2 (correct 'theirs' 845->249 island-rounds). Requiring two scans removes the phantom (1,379->0) and leaves 10340 g2 (TT 845, NT 575), 10114 g2, 9477 g2, 9903 g2, 10116 g2 and 10113 g4 unchanged.

Give mayWrite a 4-argument overload, mayWrite(age, slot, owner, confirmed), and AND the sticky clause with `confirmed`; the 3-argument form passes true, so Isle1Test is untouched. findings.title: Blind anchors are carried with no target: couriers search our half for 150 turns, return the anchor and repeat (782k carrier turns)
findings.mechanism: HQ.build allows a 'blind' anchor every ANCHOR_BLIND_PERIOD (150) rounds per HQ from r400 whenever Comms.islUnloc > 0 (HQ.java:70-71). findings.title: Island slots carry no time, so newer news more than 8 rounds old can never correct 'theirs' or 'ours' (stale for 800-1,107 rounds)
findings.mechanism: reportIsland stores (owner<<12)|enc(tile) with no time (Comms.java:257-262), and bits 14-15 are free. flushIslands lets a different owner overwrite only from a record of at most 8 rounds; an older record may fill only an EMPTY slot, up to 60 rounds old, which writes stale news (MapMem.java:175, 183-186). A writer that holds a record newer than the slot's content, but more than 8 rounds old, therefore cannot fix it. Under RULES §7 that is the normal case for islands in the enemy half. Losing one of our islands also removes the r2 4 write right beside it, so a stale 'ours' cannot be corrected on the spot either. Readers affected: islandStats (islUs and islThem feed HQ.java:68-69 and 77), Launcher.mendUpdate (Launcher.java:91; wounded launchers are sent to 'our' island), and the island hunt (Launcher.java:994-1006).
findings.evidence: 9477 g2 and 9903 g2 (Cornucopia, both round-2000 wins): island 3, beside the enemy HQ (29,7), was empty until r1017 (carrier 11558, record 29 rounds old) and r1049 (carrier 13961, 46 rounds old), when the empty-slot rule wrote 'theirs'. The enemy lost the island at r1084 and r1114, and the slot stayed 'theirs' to r2000 (917 and 887 rounds). Launcher turns on an enemy-island objective while the enemy held none: 234,518 of 351,971 (67%) and 237,225 of 349,714 (68%). 10114 g2: island 3's slot said 'ours' r797-1999 while it was enemy-held 893-1279 and neutral 1280-1999. A simulated 2-bit observation epoch with newer-wins up to 400 rounds: 9477 wrong-'theirs' 917->209; 9903 887->607; Maze 10110 g8 1,379->126; 10114 island 3 'ours'-while-not 1,108->100, with correct 'theirs' 52->340. The losses 10340 g2 and 10113 g4 were unchanged (TT 845, 898). 10116 g2 (scout-published 'theirs' at r1148, island lost r1200, stale 801 rounds) is not fixed by any write rule, because no robot that saw it neutral reached a writer.
findings.failure_scenario: We decay the enemy's home island late in the game. The slot keeps the 'theirs' that a carrier filled 30-46 rounds stale. Launchers keep an enemy-island objective; the HQs and couriers never anchor the now-neutral island, which would be the 7th of 9; the game is decided by tiebreak at r2000. findings.fix: New C.ISLE_EPOCH = false and ISLE_EPOCH_AGE = 384. Writes: reportIsland(id, owner, tile, seenRound) sets bits 14-15 to (seenRound >> 7) & 3. findings.title: Carrier census drops to a partial count at phase 32 of every 64-round epoch: a one-round build burst, and the cap of 45 does not hold
findings.mechanism: liveCarriers returns max(prevCensus, cur) for phases 0-31 and `cur` alone for phases 32-63 (Comms.java:112). A carrier ticks the census only on its first turn in write range (r2 9 of an HQ, or r2 4 of our island) in each epoch (Comms.java:94-99). At phase 32, `cur` therefore holds only the carriers that came near an HQ in the last 32 rounds. Trips take a median of 50-59 rounds and a late-game mean of 97, so `cur` falls far below the true count. The comment on lines 110-111 says it 'by then holds nearly every carrier'; that is false. On the step from max(prev, cur) to cur, every HQ sees a large free room in the same round, and HQ.build (HQ.java:94) spends it at once. C.java:37 states the intent: a 'team cap on live carriers by the Comms census'. A second effect runs the other way: in phases 0-31, max(prev, cur) still counts carriers that died during the previous epoch, so they are not replaced until phase 32.
findings.evidence: Data: matches 9901-10356, 625 games of c_eco3, c_adp1, c_gd1 and c_gx1, panel and ranked. Of 22,075 carrier builds after round 256, 8,453 (38.3%) came in the single phase-32 round, against about 345 per phase if builds were uniform (phases 28-31: 151/124/521/423; phases 34-36: 362/198/181). Against awesomelemonade 29% of builds fall in that round; against carlguo 25%. True alive carriers right after the burst (robots.csv), by our HQ count: 1 HQ median 19; 2 HQs median 38, above 45 in 20% of epochs; 3 HQs median 68 (p90 144), above 45 in 89% of epochs; 4 HQs median 83, above 45 in 97% of epochs. Forest: alive 59/76/85 at r500/800/1200; Cornucopia 58/68/105; maximum 392 (10355 g2). From r400 the cap code 'c' is 28-50% of HQ turns. On 3-4-HQ maps, 84-99% of the 'c' turns at r250-800 come while more than 45 carriers are already alive, so the cap blocks only after the overshoot and Ad banks between bursts (vs awesomelemonade 'c' is 26% of HQ turns at r300-399, and our Ad bank is 120 against their about 90). On 1-HQ maps vs strong bots, 17% of the 'c' turns come with true alive below the cap's lower bound (dead carriers still counted). Carriers then jam the wells: late carrier turns are G 39.6% and C only 15.3%; 11,851 trips spent 100 or more turns in G.
findings.failure_scenario: Forest, 4 HQs, round 544 (epoch 8, phase 32). prevCensus was 52 and cur is 18, because only 18 carriers have touched an HQ zone since round 512. Each HQ computes the room as 45 - 18 = 27 and builds carriers up to its Ad (about 5 per turn), so about 20 new carriers come out in rounds 544-545 while about 75 are already alive. They queue at the same wells (G or W for 100 or more turns), and the HQs then show 'c' for 31 rounds while Ad builds up until the next phase 32.
findings.frequency: Every game that reaches round 256 (591 of 625). The overshoot is severe on 3- and 4-HQ maps (177 games: Forest, Cornucopia, Repetition, DefaultMap) and moderate on 2-HQ maps (346 games). Estimated from robots.csv birth phases and timeline alive_C.

findings.title: The carrier room is spent once per HQ and again the next round, because new carriers reach the census only after every HQ has acted
findings.mechanism: carrierRoom (HQ.java:136) tests liveCarriers + pendingCarriers < carrierCap. pendingCarriers is a per-HQ static, reset to 0 at the start of every HQ turn (HQ.java:114). The comment there says new carriers are 'counted by the census from their first turn'. RULES.md section 4 (line 902) says new robots act next round, after everyone older. A carrier built in round r therefore ticks the census in round r+1, after all HQs have acted. Two failures follow. (1) The other HQs in round r never see this HQ's builds, so with n HQs the same room is spent n times. (2) In round r+1 the builder's own pendingCarriers is 0 again and the census still lacks the new carriers, so it spends the room a second time. Shared-array writes are immediate (RULES item 25), and HQs can always write, so nothing forces this.
findings.evidence: Builds by census phase: phase 32 8,453; phase 33 2,054 (6x the uniform 345); phase 34 362. The phase-33 echo is exactly the round in which the phase-32 carriers are not yet counted. Of 3,320 HQ-epochs with a phase-32 build, 960 also built at phase 33; Ad usually runs out first. Burst size per epoch grows with the HQ count: mean 2.2/3.8/7.1/8.2 for 1/2/3/4 HQs (p90 4/7/14/15). Alive carriers right after the burst: median 19/38/68/83, with 0%/20%/89%/97% of epochs above CAP_MAX 45.

findings.frequency: Every room opening on 2+-HQ maps (523 of 625 games), at its largest at the phase-32 burst. It also happens in phases 0-31 whenever a room opens.
findings.judge: Same sweep as the previous finding: self-play vs c_gd1 with each switch alone and both together, then CAP_MAX 45/60/75 under both, then the panel. Unit or engine-fixture test: two HQs, room 4, one round. Expect 4 carriers built in total, and none at r+1.

Each blind window also sets wantAnchor, so the 80 Ad / 80 Mn reserve holds launchers back until Mn reaches 125.

findings.title: Aura avoidance ignores the end-of-round current push, so launchers ride a current into the enemy HQ aura and loop there until they die
findings.mechanism:
Nav.can (Nav.java:60-66) checks auraStepOK(here, n, h) only for the tile n we step onto. Nav.score (Nav.java:69-76) does count n's current, and it rewards a current that pushes us toward the target.

RULES §4 end of round (RULES.md:186-194) and §6.4 (RULES.md:404-409): HQ damage (step 3) is applied before currents (step 5), and a push adds no cooldown.

What happens:
- A launcher steps onto a tile just outside r² 9.
- The current pushes it inside the aura.
- It cannot move next round (launcher move cooldown 20, RULES §5.1), so it takes aura damage and is pushed deeper.
- The AURA_SAFE step-out (Launcher.java:397-405) moves it out by one tile, still inside the aura, where it stands one more round.

findings.title: A step-in onto a cloud loses the planned shot: after the move, refreshEnemies() senses only r² 4 and drops targets whose positions are still exact
findings.mechanism:
fight() (Launcher.java:305-317) picks a tile because canHit is true: some enemy is within r² 16 of it. It ignores whether that tile is a cloud.

After rc.move, L63 re-senses (enemiesStale → refreshEnemies, L145-147). On a cloud, vision shrinks to r² 4 (RULES §6.1, RULES.md:61). Targets at r² 5-16 vanish from G.enemies, and shoot() (L166-184) fires at nothing.

But the target positions sensed at the start of our turn are still exact, because no other robot acts during our turn (RULES.md:219). A launcher attack needs no vision (RULES.md:291 lists no sensing condition; RULES.md:337: 'It can hit squares it cannot sense').

So the turn ends with an unused attack on a known target: exactly the shot the step-in was chosen for (doc L239: 'step in only to a tile that can hit something').
findings.evidence:
Per-turn launcher dumps, 33 games vs strong teams. Case: start on a clear tile, an enemy launcher visible at r² 17-20 on a clear tile, step to within r² 16.

| Destination | Ours: attacked | Theirs: attacked |
|---|---|---|
| Cloud | 14/203 (6.9%) | 147/161 hit (91%) |
| Clear | 7,292/7,306 (99.8%) | 5,979/6,007 (99.5%) |

The turn after the cloud step-in (still blind): ours hit 5/202 (2.5%), theirs 65/160 (41%).
findings.failure_scenario:
1. Our ready launcher at (x,y) sees an enemy launcher at d² 18. The tile one step closer (d² 13) is a cloud.
2. fight() scores it as a firing tile and moves there.
3. L63 refreshEnemies returns an empty array (vision r² 4), so shoot() returns.
4. The enemy, which was exactly where we sensed it, takes no damage and fires first on its own turn.
findings.frequency: About 6 lost certain shots per game vs top teams (189 of 203 step-ins in 33 games). They fall at the first contact of engagements, which decides first_hit.
findings.fix:
C.SHOOT_KNOWN (0 = c_gd1; 1 = this fix; 2 = also the next finding).

In run(), right after L56:

```java
RobotInfo[] pre = G.enemies;
```

After L63's shoot():

```java
if (C.SHOOT_KNOWN > 0 && rc.isActionReady() && rc.getRoundNum() == G.round) shootAt(pre);
```

shootAt runs shoot()'s priority / lowest-HP / lowest-id selection over pre (skipping HQs, requiring rc.canAttack(e.location)), then calls rc.attack(best.location) and shots++. To keep one code path, factor shoot()'s selection loop into a helper that takes the array.

The hit is certain: the round check excludes overrun resumes, and the positions date from this turn.
findings.judge:
1. Unit test of the selection helper (pre-move array, canAttack true at d² 13, nothing sensed).
2. Self-play vs c_gd1 on cloud-heavy maps (Forest, TimesUp and the cloud maps of the panel). Metric: attacks on the turn of a cloud step-in from the per-turn dump.
3. The panel.

findings.title: track() wipes the fighter memory on every blind turn, so a launcher that just entered a cloud never fires at enemies it saw one turn earlier
findings.mechanism:
track() L207: `if (es.length == 0) { nPinned = 0; nPrev = 0; prevRound = G.round; return; }`.

On a cloud, G.enemies is limited to r² 4 (RULES §6.1), so the first blind turn erases prevIds/prevLocs. Those are the exact positions of the fighters seen from the previous clear tile.

Nothing else remembers them. The comment at L202 says track() 'now feeds only telemetry'. Its pinned logic (L186-188) says an enemy that moved last turn cannot move this turn, so it is still on its tile, adjusted for the push by MapMem.current.

The ready launcher then ends the turn with an unused attack. A blind shot costs only action cooldown (RULES.md:291: an empty square is a legal target that takes 0), and the action is unused anyway.
findings.evidence:
Dumps, 33 games. Case: we saw an enemy launcher from a clear tile last turn, we are now on a cloud, and it is still on the same tile within r² 16.
- Ours hit 17/240 (7%). Theirs hit 290/315 (92%).

Broader view: we stand on a cloud with an enemy launcher geometrically within r² 16.
- Ours: we stayed and did not attack on 11,116 turns, against 3,236 attacks (field 6,011, near mana wells 3,154).
- Theirs: 2,370 no-attack turns vs 11,887 attacks.

All self-on-cloud turns: ours 7,465 hits on 23,097 turns, theirs 9,674 on 22,213.
findings.failure_scenario:
1. Round r-1: our launcher on a clear tile sees an enemy launcher at d² 13, fires, and kites onto a cloud.
2. Round r: es.length == 0, so track() wipes the memory. march() runs because nothing is hittable.
3. The action is ready but never used, although the enemy launcher (pinned after its own step) is still at the remembered tile.
findings.frequency: About 7 near-certain hits lost per game vs top teams (223 of 240 in 33 games). It sits inside about 337 blind no-attack cloud turns per game that we do not cover.
findings.fix:
Part of C.SHOOT_KNOWN, level 2 (≥ 2).

In track(), before the wipe at L207, when `prevRound == G.round - 1`, copy prevLocs/nPrev to memLocs/memN and set memRound = G.round - 1.

After level 1 in run():

```java
if (C.SHOOT_KNOWN > 1 && rc.isActionReady() && rc.getRoundNum() == G.round && memRound == G.round - 1
        && !hasHittableEnemies() && MapMem.cloud(G.here.x, G.here.y))
    shootMemory();
```

shootMemory:
- for each k, predict p = memLocs[k] plus the push MapMem.current(memLocs[k]);
- skip p unless rc.canAttack(p) && !rc.canSenseLocation(p);
- attack the nearest p (prefer ids that were pinned).

The memory lasts one round only, so the shots stay near-certain.
findings.judge:
1. Unit test of the memory helper: blind turn after a clear turn, with and without a current.
2. Self-play vs SHOOT_KNOWN=1 on cloud maps. Metrics: memory shots fired and hit (telemetry counter), and the engagements.csv first_hit share.
3. The panel together with level 1.

findings.title: fight()'s rand(3) beats the CENTER +1 bonus, so a launcher with its action spent and no enemy fighter in sight takes a random step one time in three
findings.mechanism:
The doc says 'Action spent: fewest threats, then staying put (moving costs the next turn's move)' (L241-242).

With ready=false and no enemy fighter in G.enemies (for example just after shooting a carrier), minD is MAX_VALUE for every tile. Then L336/L348 give every tile the same -threat*10000 + 1000.

- L352 adds 1 to CENTER, and L353 adds rand(3) (0-2) to every tile.
- CENTER (scored first, strict >) loses whenever it draws 0 and any other tile draws 2.
- P = 1/3 × (1 − (2/3)^8) ≈ 0.32 with 8 movable tiles.

The random step spends the move cooldown (20), so the launcher cannot follow the carrier next turn.
findings.evidence:
Dumps, 33 games. Case: move-ready, no enemy launcher within r² 20, a non-lethal carrier shot from the start tile.
- Ours moved 1,376/4,026 = 34%, which matches the 32% predicted for a pure tie-break.
- Our next-turn attack: 440/1,373 (32%) after moving vs 1,231/2,624 (47%) after staying.
- Theirs moved 79% and attacked next turn 63% after moving (they chase), 74% after staying.
findings.failure_scenario:
1. A launcher shoots a 40-HP carrier from its start tile, then fight() runs with ready=false.
2. All 9 tiles tie. rand gives CENTER 0 and the tile away from the carrier 2.
3. The launcher steps away, cannot move next turn, and the carrier walks out of r² 16.
findings.frequency: About 42 random steps per game vs top teams (1,376 in 33 games), costing about 6 carrier attacks per game.
findings.fix:
C.STAY_BONUS (1 = c_gd1). At L352:

```java
if (d == Direction.CENTER) s += C.STAY_BONUS;
```

- 3 puts CENTER above rand's maximum and keeps it below the 10-per-d² minD unit, so the documented 'stay on ties' holds.
- Optional level C.SPENT_CHASE = 1: when !ready and no fighter is in vision, add −10 × d² from the tile to the lowest-HP hittable non-fighter, so the launcher keeps the carrier in range. That copies theirs (63% vs our 47% after staying).
findings.judge:
1. Unit test: an all-tie fixture returns CENTER with STAY_BONUS 3.
2. Self-play vs c_gd1: carrier kills per game (deaths.csv killer_type L, type C).
3. The panel. Expect a small effect.

findings.title: C.MICRO2 is never read, and the parity hold's 'CENTER may fire' clause can never fire; the fight() doc and the C.java comment describe behaviour the code does not have
findings.mechanism:
MICRO2 (C.java:109, true; comment L107-108: 'stay when we can already hit. Off until its trial') is not referenced anywhere in src/c_gd1. The grep shows C.java only, so the parity hold at Launcher.java:337-347 is unconditional. Similarly, C.MICRO is read only by Telemetry.java:144.

In fight(), `d == Direction.CENTER ||` at L340 never applies:
- fight() runs with ready=true only when shoot() at L55 found no attackable target.
- shoot() loops while the action is ready over every non-HQ enemy with rc.canAttack, and fight's targets are a subset of those.
- So CENTER's canHit (hit0) is always false when ready.

'Stay when we can already hit' does not exist for ready=false either: L336/L348 kite toward min(minD,100). The doc at L241-242 ('Action spent: … staying put') is stale; it describes c_micro1.
findings.evidence:
grep -n MICRO2 src/c_gd1/*.java → only C.java:109. grep C.MICRO → C.java:106 and Telemetry.java:144.

Code-path proof for L340: L55 shoot() exhausts every r² 16 target while the action is ready. fight's kind 0/1 canHit uses the same G.enemies and the same r² 16.

No behavioural numbers: this finding is about wrong documentation and an ablation trap, not play.
findings.failure_scenario:
An ablation of MICRO2=false, or a 'trial' as the comment invites, compiles to an identical bot. It burns a panel run with a guaranteed null result.

The stale doc also tells a reader the launcher stays after firing, while it kites 88-93% of the time (dumps: post-shot moves ahead2 88%, par 93%).
findings.frequency: Every game; no effect on play.
findings.fix:
No behaviour change. Either:
- delete MICRO2, the L340 `d == Direction.CENTER ||` clause, and the stale doc lines (L241-242, C.java:107-108); or
- wire the switch: L328 `} else if (ahead || !C.MICRO2) {`. Default true = today; false restores g_iter0's base scoring, as the comment claims.
findings.judge: Unit test only: a parity fixture whose decision differs between MICRO2 true and false (if wired), and a check that tools/unit-tests.sh still passes. No games needed.

verdicts.title: Stale distance field is never rebuilt while a same-wave sidestep exists, so carriers sidestep and step back every turn against a wall the field thinks is open
verdicts.reason: The code path holds. Field.addWall only sets Field.stale, and Field.think never reads it. The only carrier rebuilds are Nav.java:157, reached only when go==null, and Nav.java:182, reached only after the field branch fails. When down==null and a same-wave square is free, line 145 takes the side square and line 153 returns, so the stale field is used for the rest of the game. I rebuilt the field and descent myself (verify-move/fs.py: BFS over sensed walls only, loop order i=7..0 over G.DIRS, strict < on ties). (1) 10337 g4 #10780 (born r626 at (6,27), target Ad well (9,21) per trips.csv): with knowledge from (6,27) alone, or from (6,27)+(5,25), the stale level at (5,21) is 4 against a true 13. Descent goes (5,21)->(5,20)->(5,21) on every turn. (2) 9913 g1 #10151 toward (28,9), knowledge up to r11: stale level 9 against a true 12, and it goes (28,0)->(27,0)->(28,0). With r12 knowledge added it walks out. The replay agrees. occ.py shows the W/S neighbours of (5,21) empty of robots in 955-1089 of 1110 rounds, yet unjam (state G allowed) never moved the carrier. So every turn ended with cooldown >= 10, which for an empty carrier means two moves. The proposed fix is sound. wallDown implies stale, because a wall on wave k-1 was unknown at build time. Field.request(ft,true) on the same target only rebuilds once 15 rounds have passed since startRound. For #10780 that means a rebuild at r642 instead of never. Once Field.ready is false, the second moveTwice call wall-follows until enough waves exist. The old up/same arrays referenced on that call are not changed, because think allocates new ones. Launchers already rebuild stale fields through the per-turn plan request (Launcher.java:392), so the change adds little to their behaviour.
verdicts.expected_value: medium: repeated in every Forest panel game (about 924 carrier-rounds per game) and seen in a lost ladder game (9913 PairedProgramming). The mechanism is general (a wall across the field descent, found after the field was built). It is a targeted, low-risk change. Forest panel games were already won 9/10, so the win-rate gain against strong bots is modest but real through the economy.
verdicts.frequency_check: Re-counted stuck_gd1.txt and stuck_10337.txt: carriers still on x=5 for 100+ rounds in 10/10 Forest panel games (3,2,1,3,5,3,2,1,2,8 = 30). All are in state G with bc about 3.7-4.1k (two Nav calls). trips.csv confirms #10780's target was (9,21) and that it first collected at r1746. fs.py reproduces A->B->A for 10337 #10780 and #12984 (start (5,20)) and for 9913 #10151.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Proposed fix accepted as written: in Nav.moveTo, just before line 145, `if (C.FIELD_WALL_SIDE && down == null && wallDown) { Field.stale = true; Field.request(ft, true); }`. An equivalent, slightly simpler variant: `Direction go = down != null ? down : (C.FIELD_WALL_SIDE && wallDown ? null : side);`. That reaches line 157 (a rebuild, throttled by FIELD_RESTART) and falls through to greedy/bug that same call, with no sidestep. Either way, add the unit test from the judge note: a stale field, the robot on wave k, every wave-(k-1) neighbour a known wall, one free wave-k neighbour. With the switch on, expect Field.pending after FIELD_RESTART rounds.

verdicts.title: Potions corridor plug: a mana carrier 'near' a well by straight-line distance but walled off loops W -> S -> same well forever in a 1-wide corridor, freezing 15+ units and the HQ
verdicts.reason: The W/S loop is real and observed. Within PACK_R2, packApproach sends Nav.moveTo to a collect square. That square is not Field.target, so viaField is false, and at r2 20 or less no field is ever requested (Nav.java:181). A mana carrier with no other mana well gets well=null at line 698 and re-picks (33,9). robots.csv confirms #10885 at W=963;S=159, still 1,086 rounds, and HQ s=897. Two points cut against the claimed causation and against the fix. (a) #10885 is physically immobile. From r900 to r1990 (snap2.py on r10146.pkl) its only passable neighbours are (33,11), held by #10232, and (35,11), held by launcher #10701, so its decision loop is not what holds the jam. (b) In both games the front of the plug is an Ad carrier in state G, not W: #10232 in 10146 and #12464 in 9508. Each crowd-switched from (34,9) to the walled Ad well (32,8) at r2 10-13, which is beyond PACK_R2 8, so CROWD_ROUTE never fires for it. It keeps bug-following in the corridor. (c) With CROWD_ROUTE alone, #10885's correct BFS toward (33,9) (true distance 18) has (35,11) as its only downhill square, which is the frozen launcher. The field branch therefore waits. Its same-wave side square (33,11) is the Ad carrier's. The deadlock stays.
verdicts.expected_value: low as proposed (it would most likely not clear the observed jam); medium if corrected. Potions as side A lost both recent ranked games at r2000 on islands by 1-2. A fix that sends both front carriers west would plausibly flip such games, but Potions is one ladder map and not a panel map.
verdicts.frequency_check: Both side-A Potions games since 9400 (9508 g1 vs carlguo866, 10146 g1 vs IvanGeffner) are r2000 tb_islands losses with HQ s=862/897 and 10+ units still 990-1,110 rounds. Snapshots at r900/1000/1500/1990 show the corridor (33..38,11) and the HQ-adjacent tiles frozen. The Ad front carrier is present in both games. True BFS (verify-move/fs.py): from (33,11) the downhill toward (33,9) and toward (32,8) is (32,11) (west); from (34,11) it is (35,11) (east).
verdicts.corrected_fix: Cover the G-state near-walled carrier as well as the W one, and plan to the well itself. In Carrier.gather, when Nav has been wall-following toward the current well (or a collect square of it) for N move-ready turns without getting closer, and d2(here, well) <= C.FIELD_MIN_D2, set routeWell=well and call Nav.plan(well) (Field.request(well,true); fieldOn=true; fieldFor=well). That covers states G and W. While routeWell==well, call moveTwice(well) instead of packApproach, so that viaField applies (ft.equals(t)). Clear routeWell at the well, or when the well changes. With correct fields, #10232/#12464 at (33,11)/(34,11) descend or sidestep west, (32,11) then (30,10), clearing the corridor. #10885 then sidesteps to (33,11) and also goes west. Measure it in Potions self-play from the (39,11) seat, both seats x 4 seeds.

verdicts.title: unjam() can never fire for an empty carrier that oscillates within one turn: moveTwice spends the movement cooldown that unjam requires
verdicts.reason: Real in code. An empty carrier's move costs floor(0.375*0)+5 = 5 (RULES 3.3), and ready means cd < 10, so two moves leave cd 10 and unjam returns at Carrier.java:128. stillTurns compares turn-start tiles, so an A->B->A turn counts as still. The replay is consistent: #10780's neighbours were free in about 90% of 1,110 rounds and unjam never moved it. But making unjam reachable does not rescue the cited cases. (1) Forest stale-field stall: after UNJAM_OSC's single move plus a random step, the next turn's field descent goes back down to the x=5 trap, where the side oscillation resumes, because the stale field is unchanged. (2) Potions corridor: #10232's only free neighbour on its second step is the tile it came from, so the random step returns it. #10885 has no free neighbour at all. (3) The optional anchor part of the fix does nothing. Anchor carriers (K/E/Y) take the getNumAnchors>0 branch, which returns at Carrier.java:105-107 before unjam() is called at line 116, so loosening the state check in unjam never runs for them.
verdicts.expected_value: low: the gap is real, but in the observed stalls the fix ends with the carrier back in the same trap. Any gain would come only as an add-on to FIELD_WALL_SIDE for a different, unobserved oscillation.
verdicts.frequency_check: Cooldown arithmetic checked against RULES.md (lines 60, 76, 133, 239). occ.py on r10337_g4.pkl: for (5,21), the W, S, SW and NW neighbours were empty of robots in 976, 955, 1078 and 1089 of 1110 rounds. The anchor branch's early return was confirmed by reading Carrier.run.
verdicts.corrected_fix: If kept at all, keep only the moveTwice/packApproach single-move gate (`if (C.UNJAM_OSC && stillTurns >= C.UNJAM_TURNS) return;` after the first Nav.moveTo) and drop the anchor-state clause. Anchor carriers would need an explicit unjam() call inside the anchor branch before its return. A better approach is to fix the oscillation sources (FIELD_WALL_SIDE, and corridor fields for near-walled wells) and test UNJAM_OSC only as an arm on top of them.

verdicts.title: MassiveL gridlock: crowd switches send mana carriers between the two mana wells 39 rows apart through the 2-wide west strip, and opposing streams lock 20+ carriers around well (2,0)
verdicts.reason: switchWell has no distance cap, and cross-map switches happen. trips.csv side A shows (0,39)->(2,0) 8 and 7 times and (2,0)->(0,39) 3 and 6 times in 10339 g7 and 10344 g7, mostly with S codes. That can only happen when the centre mana wells (18,14) and (21,25) are hot or unknown, since from (2,0) the well (18,14) is nearer (d2 452 against 1525). But the r700 snapshot of 10339 g7 (verify-move/strip.py) shows the gridlock is not mainly from switches. The 2-high corridor y=0..1, x=0..9 is packed with inbound G carriers that never switched (for example newborns #12899, #10303, #12742 born r608 with G=271, and #10839 G=315). They face 5 loaded R carriers on (1..3,0..1) that cannot leave east toward HQ (7,5). With SWITCH_MAX_D2=400, crowded carriers re-pick (2,0) and hold in place within r2 8 (W). They would still occupy (4,0)/(4,1), the only exits east, so the inbound-against-outbound deadlock remains. A 400 cap also removes the (2,0)->(18,14) switch (d2 452). Only the opposing streams in the strip are plausibly reduced.
verdicts.expected_value: low: 2 of 10 MassiveL panel games, both won. The cap leaves the main corridor gridlock (queue against loaded carriers) in place, and it risks cutting useful switches on Forest.
verdicts.frequency_check: Re-ran the well-change counts from trips.csv (sw.py, sw2.py), which match the finding's 8/3 and 7/6. stuck_gd1.txt has 23 and 21 'else' stalls in 10339 g7 and 10344 g7, and other MassiveL games have 0-10. The r700 corner listing has 49 of our carriers in x<=9, y<=12. Of the stalled ones in the y=0..1 corridor, about half carry S codes; the rest are inbound or loaded carriers with no switch.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Target the saturation and the passing problem rather than only switch distance. For example, a loaded carrier (R) has right of way: an empty G/W carrier adjacent to a loaded carrier that has not moved for 2+ turns steps away from the loaded carrier's HQ direction, or backs off along its own path. Also, an empty carrier queued within r2 MID_AREA-like range of a well whose collect squares are all taken counts crowdTurns (not only at d2 <= 8 or Mid sites), so the queue breaks up. If a switch cap is tried, measure it from the current well (d2(well, candidate) <= cap) and use a cap large enough to keep (2,0)->(18,14) (> 452). Test it on MassiveL and Forest self-play as the judge note suggests.

verdicts.title: Island news is published only on 1 turn in 5 at end of turn, so a fresh 'neutral' sighting brought home is lost (FLUSH_ENTRY)
verdicts.reason: Code path checked. Shared island slots get remote news only through MapMem.flushIslands. It runs when (r0+id)%5==0 at end of turn, is gated by the start-of-turn Comms.canWrite, and Comms.put re-checks the end position. scanIslands reports only islands in vision. scoutTurn fills only empty slots. tryPlace reports only the island just placed. I re-traced the cited robot in the 10114 g2 replay. Island 2 was owner 2 from r810-909 and neutral from r910. Launcher 13280 scanned from (50,24) at r932 (tile (51,28) is at d2 17, and its objective changed from 1 to 2 that turn). It ended r938 and r939 at (46,20), d2 8 to HQ (48,18), and neither was a flush turn. Its flush turns were r935 (start (48,22), d2 16, not writable) and r940. On r940 it ended at (45,21), d2 18, so the end-of-turn put was refused. One correction: at r940 the record was 8 rounds old, not 12, so it was still fresh. The write failed only because the launcher moved out of the zone before the end-of-turn flush, which is exactly what an end-of-turn entry check fixes (it would flush at the end of r938 with a 6-round-old record). Telemetry supports a phantom: from r1525 to r2000, 246,536 of 308,656 launcher turns had objective kind 1 (80%) while the enemy held no island. Other figures: 771 launchers were built (734 is L_end), and the extract has no COMMS dots (tele=bcc), so slot contents can only be simulated. The saved sim outputs show what entry flush does. 10114 g2: wrong-'theirs' 1091->81. 9477, 9903 and 10116 phantoms are unchanged (917/887/801). 10116 gains NT=100.
verdicts.expected_value: low. In the 609-game scan, all 17 games with a phantom island are wins and the 108 losses show 0 phantom launcher turns. Against strong bots, losses come from unknown enemy islands (ET 68,974, NT 15,167 island-rounds across 69 simulated losses), which this barely changes (10340 g2 TT 845->847, 10113 g4 898->898). The main effect is turning some round-2000 tiebreak wins into earlier conquest, which does not change win rate. Cost: about 23% more flush calls, bounded by the reserve guard.
verdicts.frequency_check: Replay re-trace of launcher 13280 at r925-945 and island 2 ownership (verify-state/track.py). Recount of objective kinds after r1525 from the telemetry codes (obj.py). Re-read of the V0/V7/V8 summaries and the scan.tsv phantom list (17 games, all won).
verdicts.corrected_fix: The proposed code is correct as written. One small correction: G.wasWritable starts false, so each HQ flushes once more on its first turn. That is harmless; initialise it true for HQs if exact parity matters. On its own this fixes only 1 of the 4 simulated phantom games (10114); 9477, 9903 and 10116 need the write-rule changes.

verdicts.title: ISLE_STICKY writes a single 15-round-old 'theirs' sighting over a neutral slot after the island was lost (ISLE_STICKY_CONFIRM)
verdicts.reason: The c_gd1 code matches: mayWrite's sticky clause is at MapMem:185, with ISLE_STICKY=true and ISLE_STICKY_AGE=60. c_adp1, which played 10110, has an identical MapMem.java (diffed). In the replay, island 2 was owner 2 only from r327-337. Carrier 10158 started r327 at (36,23), with tile (38,23) at d2 4, on a scan turn ((327+10158)%3==0). It was in HQ (21,21)'s zone r339-342. r342 was its flush turn, starting at (20,21) and ending at (22,20), both writable. I re-ran the slot sim (end-of-round truth): 'WRITE r342 island 2 0->2 age 15 by 10158', over a neutral slot that a carrier had filled at r263, and the slot stays 'theirs' r342-1720. With start-of-round truth no 'theirs' is ever written, so the phantom needs the enemy anchor to land before our carrier's turn in r327. Telemetry settles it independently: all 19 launchers born up to r343 took kind 2 on their first turn, and 152 of 182 born r344-700 took kind 1. V10 (two-scan) re-run: 10110 g8 T. 1379->0 and 10340 g2 unchanged (NT 575, TT 845), as claimed. Impact in that game: with c_adp1's island-deficit gate active to r1500, the phantom (islThem 1 > islUs 0) kept every HQ from building an anchor until r1500 (hq.csv: reason 'c' only until the r1525 bucket), with 600 launchers against 0 and 500-1,000 Ad banked, so conquest slipped from about r500 to r1720. In c_gd1, GATE_DEFICIT_UNTIL=800, so the same phantom would block anchors only from r400 to r800, plus the launcher misdirection.
verdicts.expected_value: low. One distinct game of 609 (9901 and 10110 replay the same game), and it was a dominant win. The fix only delays phantom writes and does not change win rate against strong bots. The losses simulated so far are unchanged.
verdicts.frequency_check: Replay trace of carrier 10158 at r322-345 and island 2 ownership. Re-ran slotsim4 V0 with end-of-round and start-of-round truth, and V10 on 10110 g8 and 10340 g2 (verify-state/v10.tsv). Newborn first-turn objective counts (verify-state/newborn.py). hq.csv anchor and reason timeline.
verdicts.corrected_fix: The fix as specified matches the simulated V10 and is correct. Note that only the sticky clause is gated: the empty-slot rule (age<=60 into an empty slot) still accepts a single-scan 'theirs', which is how island 3 was written in 9477/9903 (that island really was theirs at write time). That path is out of scope here.

verdicts.title: Blind anchors are carried with no target: couriers search our half for 150 turns, return the anchor and repeat (TAKE_NEEDS_TARGET)
verdicts.reason: Code checked. takeAnchor calls chooseIsland and takes the anchor whenever anchorTarget is null; it declines only a located target with a fresh sighting. deliverAnchor then sets state 'E' and runs scoutMove, which draws only non-enemy-side points. After ANCHOR_TIMEOUT 150 it returns the anchor ('Y'). chooseIsland skips predicted islands on the enemy side (lines 879-881). HQ.build allows blind anchors from r400 every 150 rounds when islUnloc>0. Every carrier runs censusTick, so couriers count against the carrier cap. I recounted 9479 g4 from the telemetry codes, excluding rounds with r%50==25. 166 episodes began in E: 28,893 turns, 27 found a target, 1 placed. 16 began in K: 1,377 turns, 3 placed. This matches the finding (28,891 and 1,380). E+Y totals across 609 games: wins 577,121+199,984, losses 4,375+561. Forest wins carry most of it (450,664+162,724 over 50 games). It is waste, but almost only in games already won by a wide margin (9479 g4: 315 launchers vs 1 at the end).
verdicts.expected_value: low. 99.4% of the wasted E/Y turns are in wins, and Forest losses show 0 E turns. Freeing miners in games already won does not change win rate against strong bots. The finding's alternative (enemy-side predicted targets when no sighting is nearby) is the version that could speed conquest on Forest, but c_anc3 removed exactly that because couriers were lost in Q.
verdicts.frequency_check: Recount of courier episodes in 9479 g4 with my own script (verify-state/epi.py) and with the auditor's episodes.py. E/Y aggregated by win/loss and map from scan.tsv.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Correct as proposed. One cost to note: while an anchor sits in an HQ, each empty carrier adjacent to it runs chooseIsland once per 10 rounds. That is bounded by ISLAND_LOOP_GUARD and the 3000-bytecode predicted-island guard, so there is no overrun risk.

verdicts.title: Island slots carry no time, so newer news more than 8 rounds old can never correct 'theirs' or 'ours' (ISLE_EPOCH)
verdicts.reason: The limitation is real in code: reportIsland stores owner and tile with no time, mayWrite lets only records of 8 rounds or less overwrite a different owner, and bits 14-15 are free. I verified the cited island histories in the replays. 10114 g2 island 3: ours r797-891, enemy r893-1279, neutral r1280-1999. 9477 g2 island 3: enemy r348-1083, neutral r1084 onward. The stale slot contents themselves come only from simulation, since ladder replays carry no COMMS dots. No specific robot was traced holding newer news that a writer refused, unlike findings 1-2. From the saved V5 summaries, the epoch rule helps only in part. 9477 T. 917->209, 9903 887->607, 10114 U.+UT 1108->100, but 10114's island-2 phantom gets slightly worse (T. 1091->1125). I also simulated the loss 10350 g6 (IslandHopping vs awesomelemonade). Island 7's slot says 'ours' while it is neutral from r837-1783 (947 rounds), and neither V5 nor V8 changes it, because no robot carrying the neutral news reaches a writer. The masking list for the fix is complete: Comms 147/261/264, MapMem 185, Launcher 91/884-885/899/996/998. The newer-wins proof holds: recon is never earlier than the true bucket.
verdicts.expected_value: low. The benefit is limited to won games (the 17-game phantom set) and is only partial there. It does not fix the stale-'ours' case in the loss I simulated. It is a wide change to every island-slot reader, with real regression risk for an uncertain gain.
verdicts.frequency_check: Replay ownership traces for island 3 in 10114 g2 and 9477 g2 (verify-state/i3_*.txt). Re-read of the V5/V6 outputs (v56.tsv). New V0/V5/V8 simulation of the loss 10350 g6 (verify-state/u10350_*.txt).
verdicts.corrected_fix: The design is sound as specified: 2-bit, 128-round buckets; newer-wins only when the record's bucket is above recon(slot epoch); same-owner refresh; all readers masked. One limit to note: a slot whose bucket is 4 or more buckets old reconstructs to the current bucket, so it cannot be corrected for up to 128 rounds of each 512-round cycle. That is conservative but safe. Rank it below FLUSH_ENTRY and ISLE_STICKY_CONFIRM, and test it only together with them.

verdicts.title: Carrier census drops to a partial count at phase 32 of every 64-round epoch (CENSUS_FADE)
verdicts.reason: The code path holds. Comms.liveCarriers (Comms.java:112) returns max(prevCensus, cur) in phases 0-31 and cur alone from phase 32. A carrier ticks at most once an epoch, and only while it can write (r2 9 of an HQ or r2 4 of our island). HQ.build spends the room at once. I re-ran the counts over the 616 of our games in 9901-10356 (phase.py, burst.py, alive.py). 8,413 of 21,853 carrier builds after r256 (38.5%) fall in the phase-32 round, against 341 a phase if spread evenly. The phase-32 share rises with HQ count: 26/31/39/57% for 1/2/3/4 HQs. Live carriers at phase 34 are above 45 in 65% of 3-HQ epochs and 77% of 4-HQ epochs (medians 56 and 88). The comment's premise is false. In the first 32 rounds of an epoch, only 20-43% of carriers alive through it start or end a trip (cover.py). The finding misses part of the cause, though. Over a FULL epoch only 37.5-67% do (4 HQs down to 1 HQ). On 4-HQ maps, 39% of carriers are on a single trip longer than 64 rounds (cover2.py). So prevCensus also undercounts, and no timing change makes the cap hold. In a toy model (sim.py), FADE cuts the steady-state overshoot by about 25%, and alive carriers still settle at about 1.7-2x the cap. The proposed fix has three faults. (a) FADE alone: while the fade term dominates, room = cap - fade does not see builds made since phase 32. Each HQ therefore re-spends the opening room every round until the new carriers out-tick the fade. (b) Combined with CENSUS_HQ_TICK, the HQ bump raises cur, not the fade term, so the cross-HQ double spend comes back in that stretch. (c) FADE replaces dead carriers more slowly: prev still counts them through phases 32-63. The finding claims the opposite.
verdicts.expected_value: low. The cap binds mostly in games we already win. Code 'c' is 45-49% of HQ turns after r200 in wins, but 5.9% in losses to strong bots, where 't' (threatened) is 53%. In Forest wins Ad floats at 150-625 per HQ, so the extra carriers spend no contested resource, and Mn binds (median bank 35). Earlier sweeps of CAP_MAX moved the effective cap in proportion and were neutral (c_cap1, c_eco1, c_ec01-04). Possible small gain from less congestion at wells on 3-4-HQ maps.
verdicts.frequency_check: Reproduced: phase-32 share 38.5% (auditor 38.3%); phases 28-36 counts 150/123/514/418/8413/2041/360/198/180. Mean burst per epoch with one: 2.3/3.8/7.2/8.1 for 1-4 HQs. Alive above 45 at phase 34: 3 HQs 65%, 4 HQs 77% (auditor 89%/97%, filtered to burst epochs). Census coverage proxy from deposits: half epoch 0.43/0.40/0.31/0.20, full epoch 0.67/0.63/0.53/0.375 for 1-4 HQs.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Keep the switch, but add the team's builds to the fade term so it sees them, and turn it on only together with CENSUS_HQ_TICK. In HQ, keep a per-HQ static cur32 set at phase 32 (cur32 = cur). Comms.liveCarriers: if (C.CENSUS_FADE && phase >= 32) return Math.max(cur, (prevCensus * (64 - phase) >> 5) + cur - cur32). Builds then raise both terms for every HQ at once. Old carriers ticking after phase 32 are counted twice mid-epoch, which errs toward fewer builds. Expect the effective cap to stay at about CAP_MAX / (full-epoch coverage), 1.5-2.7x nominal. To make a cap actually hold, the census must also count carriers on trips longer than 64 rounds, for example by spanning two epochs (CENSUS_HOLD) or by fixing the jams. Judge by alive_C against CAP_MAX, not only by the phase-32 share.

verdicts.title: Carrier room spent once per HQ and again the next round (CENSUS_HQ_TICK)
verdicts.reason: Both double counts hold in code. pendingCarriers is a per-robot static, reset in swarmEconomy every turn (HQ.java:114). liveCarriers is read once at turn start, from the shared census only. RULES §4 item 6: newborns act next round after every older robot, so all HQs act in round r+1 before the round-r carriers tick. In round r the other HQs never see this HQ's builds, and in round r+1 the builder sees neither its own nor theirs. Data: phase 33 has 2,041 builds (6x the even share). 949 of 3,296 HQ-epochs with a phase-32 build also built at phase 33 (birth tile assigned to the nearest HQ). The phase-32 burst grows with HQ count (2.3/3.8/7.2/8.1), as n parallel readers of one room would produce. I checked the proposed code. The epoch boundary works: a carrier born at phase 63 bumps epoch e, sets censusEpoch=e on its first turn and ticks in e+1. Bumping the previous slot in phases 0-31 moves max(prev, cur) by exactly 1. HQ 0 acts first among our HQs, so its phase-32 zeroing comes before any phase-32 bump. A newborn's first turn is in write range, since spawn tiles are within r2 9. Cost: 2 writes (about 150 bytecodes) per build, within the 20k budget. One caveat: the bump does not reach the fade term of CENSUS_FADE as proposed (see the finding above).
verdicts.expected_value: low. Same reasoning as the census-timing finding: it binds in won games and Ad floats. It removes part of the overshoot (in the toy model alive falls about 20% with tick alone), with no evidence that the overshoot costs games.
verdicts.frequency_check: Reproduced: ph33 2,041 builds (auditor 2,054); 949/3,296 HQ-epochs (auditor 960/3,320); burst means 2.3/3.8/7.2/8.1 (auditor 2.2/3.8/7.1/8.2).
verdicts.corrected_fix: As proposed (censusBuilt in HQ.java:94, plus the censusEpoch seed at Carrier.java:51). It is correct on its own. If combined with CENSUS_FADE, use the fade form max(cur, fade(prev) + cur - cur32) so the bumps lower everyone's room during the fade.

verdicts.title: Blind-anchor allowance is per HQ, not per team (BLIND_TEAM)
verdicts.reason: The behaviour is real. lastAnchorRound is a per-HQ static (HQ.java:13, 83), and the data shows it. On 4-HQ maps, half of the per-HQ gaps between anchor builds fall at 150-249 rounds (271+311+74 of 1,404). Forest wins average 16.6 builds at blind-period gaps and 19.8 at gaps under 150 (located-neutral builds). Repetition averages 32.7 at blind gaps. Forest wins build 40.6 anchors, place 6.0 and lose 1.6, so about 33 a game sit in stock or circulate, at a time when the median Mn bank is 35. Four points keep this at PLAUSIBLE. (a) The intent is unclear. C.java:91 states ANCHOR_PERIOD as per HQ ('An HQ builds at most one anchor...'), and the blind period is coded the same way. (b) The fix does not stagger the first blind window. lastAnchorRound starts at -1000, so all n HQs still build one at r400. (c) About half the Forest anchors (gaps under 150) come from located-neutral, mostly enemy-side islands, and this fix leaves them alone. (d) TAKE_NEED_TARGET (next finding) makes it nearly redundant: once a blind anchor stays in stock, getNumAnchors != 0 stops that HQ from building more and lifts the reserve. Its effect is confined to won games: in Forest losses 't' is 79% of HQ turns and 'a' 2.4%.
verdicts.expected_value: low. It frees Mn (about 12 anchors, roughly 1,000 Mn, per Forest win) in games already won. Alone it might slightly speed conquest. On top of TAKE_NEED_TARGET it adds about nothing.
verdicts.frequency_check: anchint.py/forestint.py: 4-HQ per-HQ gaps under 150: 51%; 150-249: 47%. Forest wins: first 4.0, <150 19.8, 150-249 16.6 per game; Cornucopia 9.1/8.3; Repetition 1.7/32.7. Forest built 33.6 per game (all games), as the auditor reported.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Build TAKE_NEED_TARGET first. If BLIND_TEAM is still wanted, also stagger the start, so that HQ i's first blind window opens at ANCHOR_BLIND_FROM + i * ANCHOR_BLIND_PERIOD (hqIdx is known), for example lastAnchorRound initialised on the first turn to ANCHOR_BLIND_FROM - ANCHOR_BLIND_PERIOD * (nHQ - hqIdx). Otherwise four blind anchors still appear at r400.

verdicts.title: Anchor taken with no island target: take / E-wander / return cycle (TAKE_NEED_TARGET)
verdicts.reason: The code path holds. In takeAnchor (Carrier.java:309-318), only the fresh-sighting check under anchorIsland > 0 can refuse a take; with anchorIsland == 0 the carrier still takes. deliverAnchor then sets 'E' and calls scoutMove. scoutMove makes 4 draws and keeps the first on our side at least 8 away. Only if all 4 fail does it fall back to the last draw, which may be on the enemy side. After ANCHOR_TIMEOUT the carrier returns the anchor (Y) to its nearest HQ, and the next empty carrier there takes it again. Data (ey.py): Forest wins (35) average 98.4 takes, 40.6 built, 6.0 placed, with E+Y at 10.3% of carrier turns. LookingGlass is 12.5%, Repetition 5.4%, Cornucopia wins 2.7%. In 9901 g4 there are 155 takes and 5 placed, with E 18,782 and Y 5,846 turns (14.5%). The finding's prior-attempt section is incomplete. This exact change was proposed as c_anc5 in research/diagnosis/2026-10-10-g_iter8.md (lines 678-690) and never built. Its judge (lines 979-983) put the panel effect at 0 to +1 and flagged a ReverseFunnel risk: the first RF anchor came from the r425 blind rule in 6 of 10 games. The judge suggested narrowing the gate to 'no target-less take once islUs >= 1'. ReverseFunnel today: E 205 turns a game, 2.6 placed, so the risk is smaller but still there. Implementation catch: Comms.islUs is fresh only in HQs and island scouts (islandStats). A carrier must refresh it before using it.
verdicts.expected_value: low. The leak sits almost entirely in won games; the high E+Y tiebreaks are wins (9901 g4, 9906 g4, 10115 g4, 10347 g4). It saves about 2,000+ Mn and frees 5-8 miners per long Forest win, and may speed conquest. There is little leverage on losses to strong bots, where threatened HQs build no blind anchors.
verdicts.frequency_check: Reproduced: Forest (all 43) takes 81, built 33.6, placed 5.1; Forest wins E+Y 0.103; LookingGlass 0.125; Repetition 0.054; Cornucopia 0.027. 9901 g4: T 155, E+Y 14.5%. 4 of 15 tiebreak games with E+Y > 3% were Forest wins; the 2 tiebreak losses were Marsh and Potions (6-8 anchors).
verdicts.corrected_fix: Narrowed form (c_anc5 judge), right after chooseIsland() at Carrier.java:309: if (C.TAKE_NEED_TARGET && anchorIsland == 0) { Comms.islandStats(Math.min(35, rc.getIslandCount())); if (Comms.islUs >= 1) { anchorTarget = null; return false; } }. This keeps the first blind anchor that ReverseFunnel-type maps rely on. A stocked anchor now makes every empty carrier next to that HQ run chooseIsland each turn (the prediction loop runs down to the 3,000-bytecode guard on many-island maps). Throttle it with a per-carrier static, for example retry no sooner than 10 rounds after a refusal. Optional c_anc5 part 2: a courier that is already in 'E' with no target sets anchorTurns = ANCHOR_TIMEOUT and returns the anchor at once. Judge on Forest, Repetition, Cornucopia and LookingGlass E+Y and conquest round, and check ReverseFunnel's first-anchor round on the panel.

verdicts.title: Aura avoidance ignores the end-of-round current push, so launchers ride a current into the enemy HQ aura and loop there until they die
verdicts.reason: The code path is as described. Nav.can (Nav.java:60-66) checks auraStepOK only on the step tile n, and Nav.score (69-76) rewards a current that pushes toward the target. RULES §4 step 3 and §6.4 apply HQ damage before currents, and a push adds no cooldown, so after the step the launcher cannot move next round and sits at the push tile. I decoded Forest's currents from the map (int32 vector; the existing scratchpad cur.py read it as bytes and is wrong). Columns x=53 and x=54 carry S currents from y=37 down to the B HQs at (53,30) and (52,30). (54,33) is at d²10 and pushes to (54,32) at d²5/8. The chain (54,32)→(54,31)→(54,30)→(54,29) matches the death tiles and the 8+4+4 HP cycle. Recount of 51 dumped games (the auditor's '33' merged three games per file in a1/*): 495 of our step-then-pushed-into-aura events. In 459 of them no enemy launcher or carrier was within r²20, so march/Nav.can is the main path; fight() accounts for only 36. Deaths extract ≥9400: 747 hq_aura launcher deaths; Forest A 536 in 51 of 62 games; c_gd1 alone 62 in 10 Forest-A games. Two corrections. (1) The ring hold (L446) costs no HP: a holder is move-ready next turn and leaves the aura before end of round, so that part is churn only. (2) The fight() fix as written is wrong: replacing (tx,ty) with afterPush(tx,ty) would rate an aura tile whose current pushes outward as safe, but this round's damage lands on (tx,ty) before the push.
verdicts.expected_value: low. The deaths are real but almost all happen in games we already win. Forest A: 535 of 540 aura deaths came in wins (10.5 per win vs 0.1 per loss, 1 death across 11 losses). ThirtyFive B: 83, all in 3 wins. Their launchers die in our aura 2,562 times vs our 747. The fix saves HP during sieges that are already winning and is unlikely to flip a loss; at most it speeds up some wins.
verdicts.frequency_check: v1_deaths.py: 747 total, Forest A 536 (51/62 games), hp_before 4 for 499; top tiles (54,32) 97, (54,31) 66, (55,32) 48, (53,32) 46, (55,31) 32 (reproduced). v2_build.py: c_gd1 Forest A 62 aura deaths in 10 games. v8_wl.py: Forest A wins 535 deaths in 51 games, losses 1 in 11. v7_all.py: 495 step+push-into-aura events for ours (459 with no L/C in r²20), 440 for theirs. v3_forest.py prints the Forest current columns. Scripts in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-terryvanbelle-projects-vibe-2023/4344f381-983b-4736-adb6-8d7ba2ecdeb6/scratchpad/audit/verify-combat/
verdicts.corrected_fix: Keep the Nav.can part as proposed (afterPush(n) must pass auraStepOK for every seen HQ); it covers march, the field descent and moveAway. In fight(), do not replace the tile: keep the case-2 test on (tx,ty) (this round's damage) and add, only for d != CENTER, the same aura test on Nav.afterPush(tx,ty) (next round's damage, when a launcher that just moved cannot leave). Set aura=true if either is inside and take auraD as the minimum of the two. Drop the ring-hold change or keep it optional: it saves a wasted move, not HP. Judge on Forest side A, where the cost shows up, and also count launchers alive and win round, since outcomes rarely change.

verdicts.title: A step-in onto a cloud loses the planned shot: after the move, refreshEnemies() senses only r² 4 and drops targets whose positions are still exact
verdicts.reason: fight() (L294-362) scores canHit from start-of-turn positions and never looks at clouds. After rc.move, L63 sees enemiesStale (moved) and calls refreshEnemies(), which is senseNearbyRobots(-1, them). On a cloud that sees only r²4 (RULES §6.1/6.3), so shoot() finds nothing. No robot acts during our turn (RULES §4.2) and currents apply only at end of round, so the start-of-turn positions are still exact. attack/canAttack need no vision (RULES §5.2/5.4). Recount over 51 properly split games, using map cloud flags rather than pooled positions: ours stepped in onto a cloud 258 times and attacked 4 times (1.6%), vs 7,806 of 7,823 (99.8%) onto clear tiles. Theirs attacked 274 of 274 onto clouds. The shot is lost, not deferred: the next turn is still blind.
verdicts.expected_value: low-medium. About 5 lost first-contact launcher shots per game vs top teams (254 in 51 games, not 6 per game over 33), roughly 100 damage per game at the moment that decides first hit. It costs nothing and every shot is certain.
verdicts.frequency_check: v7_all.py F2: ours stepin_cloud 258 / att 4; stepin_clear 7,823 / att 7,806; theirs stepin_cloud 274 / att 274. 51 games, not 33: the auditor's sa3.py keyed each multi-game file (top2/a1/*) on its first game, pooling 3 games and their cloud/clear sets per file.
verdicts.corrected_fix: The proposed fix is correct. Keep pre = G.enemies (start of turn; fight() does not change it, and if L55 had fired the action would not be ready). After L63's shoot(), add: if (C.SHOOT_KNOWN > 0 && rc.isActionReady() && rc.getRoundNum() == G.round) run shoot()'s selection over pre, skipping HQs and requiring rc.canAttack(e.location), then attack. Equivalent and simpler: at L63, when getRoundNum() == G.round, run shoot() on the fresh array and then on the start-of-turn array.

verdicts.title: track() wipes the fighter memory on every blind turn, so a launcher that just entered a cloud never fires at enemies it saw one turn earlier
verdicts.reason: The missing behaviour is real: c_gd1 has no shot at remembered positions. The stated cause is wrong. prevLocs/pinnedIds feed only telemetry (the L202 comment) and nothing would fire at them even without the L207 wipe, so the wipe is not the defect; the defect is a missing memory shot. The '223 of 240 near-certain hits' figure is conditioned on the outcome: it only counts enemies that did stay. Unconditional recount (51 games): 506 cases where we are on a cloud, were on a clear tile last turn, did not attack, and a launcher seen last turn is now at 4<d²≤16. The nearest one was still at its remembered tile (push included) at its next turn start in 249 (49%), and never moved in either of its own turns in 109 (22%). The turn order is unknown, so the true hit rate of a shot at the nearest remembered tile is about 22-49%. That gives about 2-5 hits per game, not 7 certain ones. Prior attempt correction: c_blind2's memory arm did not use prevLocs. It could never fire from a cloud, because blindShot requires cd + round(10×1.2)=12 ≤ 10 + MEM_DEBT and MEM_DEBT is 0. So the cloud-source case was never tested, which supports trying it.
verdicts.expected_value: low. About 2-5 extra launcher hits per game vs top teams. The blind/memory-shot family (c_blind1/c_blind2) netted +2/100 on the panel and was rejected, although that family never covered this case.
verdicts.frequency_check: v7_all.py F3: ours 506 no-attack cloud-entry cases with a launcher seen last turn in range; nearest still at its tile 249, never moved 109, any candidate stayed 266. Theirs only 32 such cases: they almost always fire.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Keep the memory separate from track()'s telemetry arrays: copy prevLocs, prevIds and pinnedIds before the L207 and L203 wipes when prevRound == G.round-1. Fire only when the action is still unused at the end of the turn and rc.getRoundNum()==G.round. Prefer ids that were pinned last turn: they cannot have moved, so their tile plus push is a certain hit. Then take the nearest p with rc.canAttack(p) && !rc.canSenseLocation(p). A shot from a cloud costs 12 cooldown, so 2 carries into the next turn and the action is still ready then. Alternative: port c_blind2's memory arm onto c_gd1 with BLIND_MEM_DEBT ≥ 2 and age 1.

verdicts.title: fight()'s rand(3) beats the CENTER +1 bonus, so a launcher with its action spent and no enemy fighter in sight takes a random step one time in three
verdicts.reason: With ready=false and no fighter in G.enemies, minD stays MAX_VALUE. L336 and L348 then give every tile -threat*10000 + 1000, and mending is off above 80 HP. CENTER (+1, scored first, needs strict >) loses only when r0=0 and some other tile draws 2: P = 1/3 × (1-(2/3)^8) = 0.320 with 8 movable tiles. G.rand(n) = (xorshift & 0x7fffffff) % n, uniform enough. Data (51 games): 1,376 of 4,025 (34.2%) moved after a non-lethal carrier shot with no enemy launcher in r²20. The next-turn attack rate was 441/1,374 (32.1%) after moving vs 1,234/2,627 (47.0%) after staying. Because the step is chosen by RNG, this comparison is close to a randomized one. The doc at L241-242 says 'staying put' on ties.
verdicts.expected_value: low. About 27 random steps per game, costing about 4 carrier attacks per game (0.149 × 1,376 / 51 ≈ 4, not 6, since the dumps hold 51 games). Small effect on enemy economy and essentially free to fix.
verdicts.frequency_check: v7_all.py F4: ours cshot 4,025, moved 1,376; moved→next att 441/1,374; still→next att 1,234/2,627. Theirs moved 3,129/3,954 with next att 63%.
verdicts.corrected_fix: STAY_BONUS 3 works in the !ready branches, which score in 10-unit steps. It also changes the ready parity fallback (rally term 3 per d²) and mendScore (3 per d²): there it turns 'one d² closer to rally/mend tile' into a coin flip with CENTER. To make it a pure tie-break, use: if (d == Direction.CENTER) s += (!ready && !(C.MEND && mending)) ? C.STAY_BONUS : 1;

verdicts.title: C.MICRO2 is never read, and the parity hold's 'CENTER may fire' clause can never fire; the fight() doc and the C.java comment describe behaviour the code does not have
verdicts.reason: grep finds MICRO2 only at C.java:109 and C.MICRO only at C.java:106 and Telemetry.java:144. When fight() runs with ready=true, shoot() at L55 has exited its while(isActionReady) loop with best==null. Its SHOOT_GUARD break needs best!=null, so no non-HQ enemy in G.enemies is within r²16. fight()'s kind 0/1 targets are a subset of that array, measured from the same tile. So CENTER's canHit is false and `d == Direction.CENTER ||` at L340 is dead (except after an overrun resume, a basics violation). The C.java:107-108 comment ('stay when we can already hit. Off until its trial') contradicts the value true. L241-242 ('Action spent: … staying put') contradicts L336/L348, which kite by min(minD,100)*10.
verdicts.expected_value: none for win rate. This is documentation and ablation hygiene: it prevents a wasted panel run on a MICRO2=false build that would compile to an identical bot.
verdicts.frequency_check: Static check; no game numbers are needed. The dump's post-shot kite shares (ahead2 88% moved, par 93%) are consistent with the code, not the doc.
verdicts.corrected_fix: As proposed. Either delete MICRO2, the L340 CENTER clause and the stale doc lines, or wire `} else if (ahead || !C.MICRO2) {` at L328. Prefer deletion: re-enabling base scoring was already measured (arch_swarm).
